PMF.comment:
A probability mass function, or discrete probability measures is a function `α → ℝ≥0∞` such
that the values have (infinite) sum `1`.

explanatories.HasSum: An infinite sum on a topological monoid is defined as the limit of sums over increasingly larger finite subsets, and this sum operation is robust against reordering of terms.

PMF.fullDefinition: def PMF.{u} (α : Type u) : Type u :=   { f : α → ℝ≥0∞ // HasSum f 1 }
PMF.description: A probability mass function is defined as a function that maps elements of a specified type to non-negative real numbers, ensuring that the total sum of its values equals one.

PMF.toMeasure.comment:

explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.

ProbabilityTheory.preCDF.code: ProbabilityTheory.preCDF.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {mα : MeasurableSpace α} (ρ : Measure (α × ℝ)) (r : ℚ) : α → ℝ≥0∞
ProbabilityTheory.preCDF.comment:
`preCDF` is the Radon-Nikodym derivative of `ρ.IicSnd` with respect to `ρ.fst` at each
`r : ℚ`. This function `ℚ → α → ℝ≥0∞` is such that for almost all `a : α`, the function `ℚ → ℝ≥0∞`
satisfies the properties of a cdf (monotone with limit 0 at -∞ and 1 at +∞, right-continuous).

We define this function on `ℚ` and not `ℝ` because `ℚ` is countable, which allows us to prove
properties of the form `∀ᵐ a ∂ρ.fst, ∀ q, P (preCDF q a)`, instead of the weaker
`∀ q, ∀ᵐ a ∂ρ.fst, P (preCDF q a)`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.IsFiniteMeasure.Ii: This theorem demonstrates that if a measure is finite over a product space, then the measure restricted to a set defined by an interval is also finite.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv: This definition describes a measurable function that represents the Radon-Nikodym derivative of one measure with respect to another, returning this derivative function or the zero function if no decomposition exists.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.density.comment:
Density of the kernel `κ` with respect to `ν`. This is a function `α → γ → Set β → ℝ` which
is measurable on `α × γ` for all measurable sets `s : Set β` and satisfies that

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.borelMarkovFrom.comment:
Auxiliary definition for `ProbabilityTheory.kernel.condKernel`.
A Borel space `Ω` embeds measurably into `ℝ` (with embedding `e`), hence we can get a `kernel α Ω`
from a `kernel α ℝ` by taking the comap by `e`.
Here we take the comap of a modification of `η : kernel α ℝ`, useful when `η a` is a probability
measure with all its mass on `range e` almost everywhere with respect to some measure and we want to
ensure that the comap is a Markov kernel.
We thus take the comap by `e` of a kernel defined piecewise: `η` when
`η a (range (embeddingReal Ω))ᶜ = 0`, and an arbitrary deterministic kernel otherwise.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProd_fst_bo.comment:

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.condKernelCount.fullDefinition: def condKernelCountable (κ : kernel α (β × Ω)) [IsFiniteKernel κ] : kernel (α × β) Ω where   val p := (κ p.1).condKernel p.2   property := by     change Measurable ((fun q : β × α ↦ (κ q.2).condKernel q.1) ∘ Prod.swap)     refine (measurable_from_prod_countable' (fun a ↦ ?_) ?_).comp measurable_swap     · exact kernel.measurable (κ a).condKernel     · intro y y' x hy'       have : κ y' = κ y := by         ext s hs         exact mem_of_mem_measurableAtom hy'           (kernel.measurable_coe κ hs (measurableSet_singleton (κ y s))) rfl       simp [this]

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.code:

  AddSubmonoid (α → Measure β)
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.comment:
A kernel from a measurable space `α` to another measurable space `β` is a measurable function
`κ : α → Measure β`. The measurable space structure on `MeasureTheory.Measure β` is given by
`MeasureTheory.Measure.instMeasurableSpace`. A map `κ : α → MeasureTheory.Measure β` is measurable
iff `∀ s : Set β, MeasurableSet s → Measurable (fun a ↦ κ a s)`.

explanatories.Measurable: This definition describes a function between measurable spaces as measurable if it preserves the measurability of sets by ensuring that the preimage of any measurable set is also measurable.
explanatories.Measurable.add: The theorem demonstrates that the product of two measurable functions is also measurable in a specified measurable space.
explanatories.measurable_zero: The constant function mapping to one is measurable within the context of given measurable spaces.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.fullDefinition: noncomputable def kernel (α β : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β] :     AddSubmonoid (α → Measure β) where   carrier := Measurable   zero_mem' := measurable_zero   add_mem' hf hg := Measurable.add hf hg
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.description: This definition introduces the concept of a kernel as a measurable function that assigns a measure on one space for each point in another measurable space.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProdFun.comment:
Auxiliary function for the definition of the composition-product of two kernels.
For all `a : α`, `compProdFun κ η a` is a countably additive function with value zero on the empty
set, and the composition-product of kernels is defined in `kernel.compProd` through
`Measure.ofMeasurable`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProdFun.fullDefinition: noncomputable def compProdFun (κ : kernel α β) (η : kernel (α × β) γ) (a : α) (s : Set (β × γ)) :     ℝ≥0∞ :=   ∫⁻ b, η (a, b) {c | (b, c) ∈ s} ∂κ a
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProdFun.description: This definition introduces an auxiliary function that computes a specific countably additive measure related to the composition-product of two kernels at a given point, returning a non-negative extended real number.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProd.comment:
Composition-Product of kernels. For s-finite kernels, it satisfies
`∫⁻ bc, f bc ∂(compProd κ η a) = ∫⁻ b, ∫⁻ c, f (b, c) ∂(η (a, b)) ∂(κ a)`
(see `ProbabilityTheory.kernel.lintegral_compProd`).
If either of the kernels is not s-finite, `compProd` is given the junk value 0.

The pushforward of a kernel along a measurable function.

to make sure that typeclass inference can infer that the `map` of a Markov kernel
is again a Markov kernel.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.comap.comment:
Pullback of a kernel, such that for each set s `comap κ g hg c s = κ (g c) s`.
We include measurability in the assumptions instead of using junk values
to make sure that typeclass inference can infer that the `comap` of a Markov kernel
is again a Markov kernel.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.withDensity.code:
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.withDensity.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {mα : MeasurableSpace α}
  {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} (κ : ↥(kernel α β)) [IsSFiniteKernel κ] (f : α → β → ℝ≥0∞) : ↥(kernel α β)
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.withDensity.comment:
Kernel with image `(κ a).withDensity (f a)` if `Function.uncurry f` is measurable, and
with image 0 otherwise. If `Function.uncurry f` is measurable, it satisfies
`∫⁻ b, g b ∂(withDensity κ f hf a) = ∫⁻ b, f a b * g b ∂(κ a)`.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.withDensity.fullDefinition: noncomputable def withDensity (κ : kernel α β) [IsSFiniteKernel κ] (f : α → β → ℝ≥0∞) :     kernel α β :=   @dite _ (Measurable (Function.uncurry f)) (Classical.dec _) (fun hf =>     (⟨fun a => (κ a).withDensity (f a),       by         refine Measure.measurable_of_measurable_coe _ fun s hs => ?_         simp_rw [withDensity_apply _ hs]         exact hf.setLIntegral_kernel_prod_right hs⟩ : kernel α β)) fun _ => 0
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.withDensity.description: This definition introduces a kernel that adjusts the density of another kernel based on a measurable function, resulting in a new kernel with modified images.

  {E : Type u_4} {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} {mγ : MeasurableSpace γ} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {κ : ↥(kernel α β)} [IsSFiniteKernel κ] {η : ↥(kernel (α × β) γ)} [IsSFiniteKernel η] {a : α} ⦃f : β × γ → E⦄
  (h1f : StronglyMeasurable f) :
  HasFiniteIntegral f ((κ ⊗ₖ η) a) ↔
    (∀ᵐ (x : β) ∂κ a, HasFiniteIntegral (fun y => f (x, y)) (η (a, x))) ∧
      HasFiniteIntegral (fun x => ∫ (y : γ), ‖f (x, y)‖ ∂η (a, x)) (κ a)

explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.kernel.compProd: This definition introduces a new kernel that represents the composition-product of two kernels, which results in a kernel from the first type to a product type, provided the kernels are s-finite, with specific integral properties if they are not, yielding a default value of zero.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.rnDerivAux.comment:
Auxiliary function used to define `ProbabilityTheory.kernel.rnDeriv` and
`ProbabilityTheory.kernel.singularPart`.

This has the properties we want for a Radon-Nikodym derivative only if `κ ≪ ν`. The definition of

  [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω] :
  {x : MeasurableSpace α} →
    [inst : MeasurableSpace β] → (α → Ω) → (α → β) → (μ : Measure α) → [inst_1 : IsFiniteMeasure μ] → ↥(kernel β Ω)
ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib.comment:
**Regular conditional probability distribution**: kernel associated with the conditional
expectation of `Y` given `X`.
For almost all `a`, `condDistrib Y X μ` evaluated at `X a` and a measurable set `s` is equal to
the conditional expectation `μ⟦Y ⁻¹' s | mβ.comap X⟧ a`. It also satisfies the equality
`μ[(fun a => f (X a, Y a)) | mβ.comap X] =ᵐ[μ] fun a => ∫ y, f (X a, y) ∂(condDistrib Y X μ (X a))`
for all integrable functions `f`.

ProbabilityTheory.setLIntegral_preimage_.code:
ProbabilityTheory.setLIntegral_preimage_condDistrib.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {Ω : Type u_3}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω] {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {X : α → β} {Y : α → Ω} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} {s : Set Ω} {t : Set β} (hX : Measurable X) (hY : AEMeasurable Y μ)
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) :
  ∫⁻ (a : α) in X ⁻¹' t, ((condDistrib Y X μ) (X a)) s ∂μ = μ (X ⁻¹' t ∩ Y ⁻¹' s)

ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_cond.code:
ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_condexp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {Ω : Type u_3}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω] {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {X : α → β} {Y : α → Ω} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} {s : Set Ω} (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y)
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
  (fun a => (((condDistrib Y X μ) (X a)) s).toReal) =ᶠ[ae μ]
    μ[(Y ⁻¹' s).indicator fun ω => 1|MeasurableSpace.comap X mβ]
ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_cond.comment:
For almost every `a : α`, the `condDistrib Y X μ` kernel applied to `X a` and a measurable set
`s` is equal to the conditional expectation of the indicator of `Y ⁻¹' s`.

explanatories.MeasurableSpace.comap: This definition describes a measurable space constructed from an existing measurable space by considering the preimages of measurable sets under a function, ensuring that a set is measurable if it corresponds to the preimage of a measurable set in the target space.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.ae: The "almost everywhere" filter represents the collection of sets that differ from a given set by at most a collection of co-null sets.

ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_cond.description: This theorem states that for almost every input, the conditional distribution of one variable given another equals the conditional expectation of the indicator function of a measurable set associated with the first variable.

ProbabilityTheory.condexpKernel.code:
ProbabilityTheory.condexpKernel.{u_3} {Ω : Type u_3} [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω]
  (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (m : MeasurableSpace Ω) : ↥(kernel Ω Ω)
ProbabilityTheory.condexpKernel.comment:
Kernel associated with the conditional expectation with respect to a σ-algebra. It satisfies
`μ[f | m] =ᵐ[μ] fun ω => ∫ y, f y ∂(condexpKernel μ m ω)`.
It is defined as the conditional distribution of the identity given the identity, where the second
identity is understood as a map from `Ω` with the σ-algebra `mΩ` to `Ω` with σ-algebra `m ⊓ mΩ`.
We use `m ⊓ mΩ` instead of `m` to ensure that it is a sub-σ-algebra of `mΩ`. We then use
`kernel.comap` to get a kernel from `m` to `mΩ` instead of from `m ⊓ mΩ` to `mΩ`.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.measurable_id'': If one measurable space is contained within another, then the identity function on that space is also measurable.
explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.kernel.comap: This definition describes a pullback operation on a kernel, producing a new kernel that is compatible with measurable functions by ensuring the measurability of the resulting transformation.
explanatories.inf_le_left: The infimum of two elements is less than or equal to the first element.

ProbabilityTheory.condexpKernel.fullDefinition: noncomputable irreducible_def condexpKernel (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]     (m : MeasurableSpace Ω) : @kernel Ω Ω m mΩ :=   kernel.comap (@condDistrib Ω Ω Ω mΩ _ _ mΩ (m ⊓ mΩ) id id μ _) id     (measurable_id'' (inf_le_left : m ⊓ mΩ ≤ m))
ProbabilityTheory.condexpKernel.description: This definition describes a kernel that represents the conditional expectation given a specific σ-algebra, ensuring that the resulting conditional distribution adheres to the associated measurable structures.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.iIndepSets.comment:
A family of sets of sets `π : ι → Set (Set Ω)` is independent with respect to a kernel `κ` and
a measure `μ` if for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n`, then `∀ᵐ a ∂μ, κ a (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, κ a (f i)`.
It will be used for families of pi_systems.
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.iIndepSets.fullDefinition: def iIndepSets {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}     (π : ι → Set (Set Ω)) (κ : kernel α Ω) (μ : Measure α := by volume_tac) : Prop :=   ∀ (s : Finset ι) {f : ι → Set Ω} (_H : ∀ i, i ∈ s → f i ∈ π i),   ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, κ a (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, κ a (f i)
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.iIndepSets.description: This definition characterizes a family of sets as independent in the context of a specific kernel and measure by a condition involving the intersection of sets and their product measures.

ProbabilityTheory.kernel.IndepSets.comment:
Two sets of sets `s₁, s₂` are independent with respect to a kernel `κ` and a measure `μ` if for
any sets `t₁ ∈ s₁, t₂ ∈ s₂`, then `∀ᵐ a ∂μ, κ a (t₁ ∩ t₂) = κ a (t₁) * κ a (t₂)`
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.IndepSets.fullDefinition: def IndepSets {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}     (s1 s2 : Set (Set Ω)) (κ : kernel α Ω) (μ : Measure α := by volume_tac) : Prop :=   ∀ t1 t2 : Set Ω, t1 ∈ s1 → t2 ∈ s2 → (∀ᵐ a ∂μ, κ a (t1 ∩ t2) = κ a t1 * κ a t2)
ProbabilityTheory.kernel.IndepSets.description: This definition describes the independence of two sets of sets in relation to a kernel and measure by a condition involving their joint measure being equal to the product of their individual measures.

  (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop
ProbabilityTheory.iIndepSets.comment:
A family of sets of sets `π : ι → Set (Set Ω)` is independent with respect to a measure `μ` if
for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n`, then `μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i) `.
It will be used for families of pi_systems.

  (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop
ProbabilityTheory.iIndep.comment:
A family of measurable space structures (i.e. of σ-algebras) is independent with respect to a
measure `μ` (typically defined on a finer σ-algebra) if the family of sets of measurable sets they
define is independent. `m : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω` is independent with respect to measure `μ` if
for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ m i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ m i_n`, then `μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i)`.

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.indepFun_fin.comment:
If `f` is a family of mutually independent random variables (`iIndepFun m f μ`) and `S, T` are
two disjoint finite index sets, then the tuple formed by `f i` for `i ∈ S` is independent of the

ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets.code:
ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} (m' : MeasurableSpace Ω)
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (hm' : m' ≤ mΩ) (π : ι → Set (Set Ω))
  (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] : Prop
ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets.comment:
A family of sets of sets `π : ι → Set (Set Ω)` is conditionally independent given `m'` with
respect to a measure `μ` if for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n`, then `μ⟦⋂ i in s, f i | m'⟧ =ᵐ[μ] ∏ i ∈ s, μ⟦f i | m'⟧`.
See `ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets_iff`.
It will be used for families of pi_systems.

explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.kernel.iIndepSets: This definition characterizes a family of sets as independent in the context of a specific kernel and measure by a condition involving the intersection of sets and their product measures.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.trim: This definition describes how to restrict a measure to a smaller σ-algebra within a measurable space.
explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.kernel.iIndep.iIndepSe: This theorem establishes that if a collection of measurable spaces is independent with respect to a kernel and measure, then the corresponding collection of sets generated from these measurable spaces also maintains that independence.

ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets.fullDefinition: def iCondIndepSets (π : ι → Set (Set Ω)) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :     Prop :=   kernel.iIndepSets π (condexpKernel μ m') (μ.trim hm')
ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets.description: This definition establishes the concept of conditional independence for a family of sets given a measurable space and a measure, which involves the equality of the measure of the intersection of sets and the product of their individual measures under the stated conditions.

ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepSets.comment:
Two sets of sets `s₁, s₂` are conditionally independent given `m'` with respect to a measure
`μ` if for any sets `t₁ ∈ s₁, t₂ ∈ s₂`, then `μ⟦t₁ ∩ t₂ | m'⟧ =ᵐ[μ] μ⟦t₁ | m'⟧ * μ⟦t₂ | m'⟧`.
See `ProbabilityTheory.condIndepSets_iff`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.trim: This definition describes how to restrict a measure to a smaller σ-algebra within a measurable space.
explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.kernel.IndepSets: This definition describes the independence of two sets of sets in relation to a kernel and measure by a condition involving their joint measure being equal to the product of their individual measures.

ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepSets.fullDefinition: def CondIndepSets (s1 s2 : Set (Set Ω)) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :     Prop :=   kernel.IndepSets s1 s2 (condexpKernel μ m') (μ.trim hm')
ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepSets.description: This definition characterizes the conditional independence of two collections of sets given a measurable space and a measure, asserting a specific relationship between the measures of intersections and the individual sets.

ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets_iff.code:
ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepSets_iff.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} (m' : MeasurableSpace Ω)
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [StandardBorelSpace Ω] [Nonempty Ω] (hm' : m' ≤ mΩ) (π : ι → Set (Set Ω))
  (hπ : ∀ (i : ι), ∀ s ∈ π i, MeasurableSet s) (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :
  iCondIndepSets m' hm' π μ ↔
    ∀ (s : Finset ι) {f : ι → Set Ω},
      (∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ π i) →
        μ[(⋂ i ∈ s, f i).indicator fun ω => 1|m'] =ᶠ[ae μ] ∏ i ∈ s, μ[(f i).indicator fun ω => 1|m']

ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndep.comment:
A family of measurable space structures (i.e. of σ-algebras) is conditionally independent given
`m'` with respect to a measure `μ` (typically defined on a finer σ-algebra) if the family of sets of
measurable sets they define is independent. `m : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω` is conditionally independent
given `m'` with respect to measure `μ` if for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for
any sets `f i_1 ∈ m i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ m i_n`, then
`μ⟦⋂ i in s, f i | m'⟧ =ᵐ[μ] ∏ i ∈ s, μ⟦f i | m'⟧ `.
See `ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndep_iff`.

spaces, each with a measurable space structure, is conditionally independent if the family of
measurable space structures they generate on `Ω` is conditionally independent. For a function `g`

ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepFun.description: This definition describes a concept of conditional independence for a family of functions that map from a common space to potentially different measurable spaces, asserting that their generated measurable structures on the common space are conditionally independent.

If a random variable `f` in `ℝ≥0∞` is independent of an event `T`, then if you restrict the
random variable to `T`, then `E[f * indicator T c 0]=E[f] * E[indicator T c 0]`. It is useful for
`lintegral_mul_eq_lintegral_mul_lintegral_of_independent_measurableSpace`.

ProbabilityTheory.lintegral_mul_eq_lintegral_mul_lintegral_of_independent_measurableSpace.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {f g : Ω → ℝ≥0∞} {Mf Mg mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} (hMf : Mf ≤ mΩ) (hMg : Mg ≤ mΩ)
  (h_ind : Indep Mf Mg μ) (h_meas_f : Measurable f) (h_meas_g : Measurable g) :
  ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), f ω * g ω ∂μ = (∫⁻ (ω : Ω), f ω ∂μ) * ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), g ω ∂μ
ProbabilityTheory.lintegral_mul_eq_linte.comment:
If `f` and `g` are independent random variables with values in `ℝ≥0∞`,
then `E[f * g] = E[f] * E[g]`. However, instead of directly using the independence
of the random variables, it uses the independence of measurable spaces for the
domains of `f` and `g`. This is similar to the sigma-algebra approach to
independence. See `lintegral_mul_eq_lintegral_mul_lintegral_of_indepFun` for
a more common variant of the product of independent variables.

ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_iff_integral_.code:
ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_iff_integral_comp_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
  [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {β : Type u_2} {β' : Type u_3} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} {mβ' : MeasurableSpace β'} {f : Ω → β}
  {g : Ω → β'} {hfm : Measurable f} {hgm : Measurable g} :
  IndepFun f g μ ↔
    ∀ {φ : β → ℝ} {ψ : β' → ℝ},
      Measurable φ →
        Measurable ψ →
          Integrable (φ ∘ f) μ →
            Integrable (ψ ∘ g) μ → integral μ (φ ∘ f * ψ ∘ g) = integral μ (φ ∘ f) * integral μ (ψ ∘ g)
ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_iff_integral_.comment:
Independence of functions `f` and `g` into arbitrary types is characterized by the relation
`E[(φ ∘ f) * (ψ ∘ g)] = E[φ ∘ f] * E[ψ ∘ g]` for all measurable `φ` and `ψ` with values in `ℝ`
satisfying appropriate integrability conditions.

MeasureTheory.pdf.integral_pdf_smul.code:
MeasureTheory.pdf.integral_pdf_smul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace E]
  {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} {ℙ : Measure Ω} {μ : Measure E} {F : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [IsFiniteMeasure ℙ] {X : Ω → E} [HasPDF X ℙ μ] {f : E → F} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
  ∫ (x : E), (pdf X ℙ μ x).toReal • f x ∂μ = ∫ (x : Ω), f (X x) ∂ℙ
MeasureTheory.pdf.integral_pdf_smul.comment:
**The Law of the Unconscious Statistician**: Given a random variable `X` and a measurable
function `f`, `f ∘ X` is a random variable with expectation `∫ x, pdf X x • f x ∂μ`
where `μ` is a measure on the codomain of `X`.

MeasureTheory.pdf.integral_pdf_smul.description: This theorem states that the integral of a measurable function scaled by the probability density function of a random variable equals the integral of that function evaluated at the random variable, assuming the function is strongly measurable.

  [HasPDF X ℙ μ] (hX : AEMeasurable X ℙ) {g : E → F} (hg : QuasiMeasurePreserving g μ ν)
  (hmap : (map g (map X ℙ)).HaveLebesgueDecomposition ν) : HasPDF (g ∘ X) ℙ ν
MeasureTheory.pdf.quasiMeasurePreserving.comment:
A random variable that `HasPDF` transformed under a `QuasiMeasurePreserving`
map also `HasPDF` if `(map g (map X ℙ)).HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ`.

`quasiMeasurePreserving_hasPDF` is more useful in the case we are working with a
probability measure and a real-valued random variable.

MeasureTheory.pdf.quasiMeasurePreserving.description: This theorem states that if a random variable has a probability density function and is transformed through a quasi-measure-preserving map, then the composition of the random variable and the map also has a probability density function with respect to the original measure.

  {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : AEMeasurable X ℙ) : HasPDF X ℙ volume ↔ map X ℙ ≪ volume
Real.hasPDF_iff_of_aemeasurable.comment:
A real-valued random variable `X` `HasPDF X ℙ λ` (where `λ` is the Lebesgue measure) if and
only if the push-forward measure of `ℙ` along `X` is absolutely continuous with respect to `λ`.

`∫ x, x * f x ∂λ` where `λ` is the Lebesgue measure.

explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.PMF.ofFinset: A probability mass function can be constructed from a finite set and a function that assigns non-negative values summing to one on that set while assigning zero outside of it.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Finset.sum_ite_mem: The theorem states that the sum of a function applied over a finite set can be expressed in terms of the sum over a subset of that set, where each element is conditionally counted based on its membership in another specified set.
explanatories.Finset.inter_self: This theorem asserts that the intersection of a finite set with itself is equal to the original set.
explanatories.Finset.sum_const: The theorem establishes that the sum of a constant value over a finite set equals the product of the constant value and the cardinality of that set.
explanatories.nsmul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a natural number with an element of a non-associative semiring is equivalent to the multiplication of that natural number cast into the semiring with the element.
explanatories.Nat.cast_eq_zero: This theorem demonstrates that in a type with characteristic zero and an additive monoid with a unity element, the equality of the image of a natural number under the canonical map to zero is equivalent to the natural number itself being zero.
explanatories.Finset.card_eq_zero: This theorem states that the cardinality of a finite set is zero if and only if the set is empty.
explanatories.Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty: This theorem states that a finite set is nonempty if and only if it is not the empty set.
explanatories.ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel: This theorem asserts that for a nonzero and finite extended nonnegative real number, the product of the number and its reciprocal equals one.
explanatories.ENNReal.natCast_ne_top: This theorem states that the embedding of any natural number into the extended nonnegative reals is not equal to the top element.
explanatories.if_false: This theorem indicates that when the condition is always false, the result of a conditional expression will equal the second option unconditionally.
explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.Multiset.card: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.
explanatories.Multiset.card_eq_zero: This theorem states that a multiset has a cardinality of zero if and only if it is empty.

PMF.uniformOfFinset.fullDefinition: def uniformOfFinset (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) : PMF α := by   refine ofFinset (fun a => if a ∈ s then s.card⁻¹ else 0) s ?_ ?_   · simp only [Finset.sum_ite_mem, Finset.inter_self, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]     have : (s.card : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by       simpa only [Ne, Nat.cast_eq_zero, Finset.card_eq_zero] using         Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.1 hs     exact ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel this <| ENNReal.natCast_ne_top s.card   · exact fun x hx => by simp only [hx, if_false]

pmf.uniform_of_finset.fullDefinition: def uniformOfFinset (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) : PMF α := by   refine ofFinset (fun a => if a ∈ s then s.card⁻¹ else 0) s ?_ ?_   · simp only [Finset.sum_ite_mem, Finset.inter_self, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]     have : (s.card : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by       simpa only [Ne, Nat.cast_eq_zero, Finset.card_eq_zero] using         Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.1 hs     exact ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel this <| ENNReal.natCast_ne_top s.card   · exact fun x hx => by simp only [hx, if_false]

ProbabilityTheory.cdf.comment:
Cumulative distribution function of a real measure. The definition currently makes sense only
for probability measures. In that case, it satisfies `cdf μ x = (μ (Iic x)).toReal` (see
`ProbabilityTheory.cdf_eq_toReal`).

explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.condCDF: This definition introduces the conditional cumulative distribution function of a measure with respect to a given value, represented as a Stieltjes function.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac: This definition establishes a Dirac measure that assigns a total measure of one to a specified point in a measurable space and zero to all other points.
explanatories.Unit.unit: This defines a unique element of the unit type, which is a type that has only one possible value.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.prod: This definition describes the construction of a measure for the Cartesian product of two measurable spaces, based on two given measures, where at least one measure is required to be s-finite.

ProbabilityTheory.cdf.fullDefinition: def cdf (μ : Measure ℝ) : StieltjesFunction :=   condCDF ((Measure.dirac Unit.unit).prod μ) Unit.unit
ProbabilityTheory.cdf.description: This definition outlines the cumulative distribution function associated with a real-valued measure, specifically applicable to probability measures.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.code:

  {E : Type u_4} [Zero E] [TopologicalSpace E] (f : ι → Ω → E) (ℱ : Filtration ι m) (μ : Measure Ω) : Ω → E
MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.comment:
Given a process `f` and a filtration `ℱ`, if `f` converges to some `g` almost everywhere and
`g` is `⨆ n, ℱ n`-measurable, then `limitProcess f ℱ μ` chooses said `g`, else it returns 0.

This definition is used to phrase the a.e. martingale convergence theorem
`Submartingale.ae_tendsto_limitProcess` where an L¹-bounded submartingale `f` adapted to `ℱ`
converges to `limitProcess f ℱ μ` `μ`-almost everywhere.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.fullDefinition: noncomputable def limitProcess (f : ι → Ω → E) (ℱ : Filtration ι m)     (μ : Measure Ω) :=   if h : ∃ g : Ω → E,     StronglyMeasurable[⨆ n, ℱ n] g ∧ ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n ω) atTop (𝓝 (g ω)) then   Classical.choose h else 0
MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.description: This definition establishes a process that, given a converging function and a filtration, either selects the limit function that is measurable with respect to the filtration or returns a default value of zero.

MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.eq.code:
MeasureTheory.Filtration.limitProcess.eq_1.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_3} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  [Preorder ι] {E : Type u_4} [Zero E] [TopologicalSpace E] (f : ι → Ω → E) (ℱ : Filtration ι m) (μ : Measure Ω) :

MeasureTheory.ProgMeasurable.comment:
Progressively measurable process. A sequence of functions `u` is said to be progressively
measurable with respect to a filtration `f` if at each point in time `i`, `u` restricted to
`Set.Iic i × Ω` is measurable with respect to the product `MeasurableSpace` structure where the
σ-algebra used for `Ω` is `f i`.
The usual definition uses the interval `[0,i]`, which we replace by `Set.Iic i`. We recover the
usual definition for index types `ℝ≥0` or `ℕ`.

explanatories.MeasurableSpace.prod: A measurable space can be constructed for the Cartesian product of two measurable spaces, allowing for the analysis of functions defined on pairs of elements from those spaces.
explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.

measure_theory.prog_measurable.comment:
Progressively measurable process. A sequence of functions `u` is said to be progressively
measurable with respect to a filtration `f` if at each point in time `i`, `u` restricted to
`Set.Iic i × Ω` is measurable with respect to the product `MeasurableSpace` structure where the
σ-algebra used for `Ω` is `f i`.
The usual definition uses the interval `[0,i]`, which we replace by `Set.Iic i`. We recover the
usual definition for index types `ℝ≥0` or `ℕ`.

MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime.{u_1, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_3} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} [Preorder ι]
  (f : Filtration ι m) (τ : Ω → ι) : Prop
MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime.comment:
A stopping time with respect to some filtration `f` is a function
`τ` such that for all `i`, the preimage of `{j | j ≤ i}` along `τ` is measurable
with respect to `f i`.

Intuitively, the stopping time `τ` describes some stopping rule such that at time
`i`, we may determine it with the information we have at time `i`.
MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime.fullDefinition: def IsStoppingTime [Preorder ι] (f : Filtration ι m) (τ : Ω → ι) :=   ∀ i : ι, MeasurableSet[f i] <| {ω | τ ω ≤ i}
MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime.description: This definition characterizes a stopping time in the context of a filtration as a function that allows for the determination of its value at any time based on the information available up to that time, which must be measurable with respect to the filtration at that index.

MeasureTheory.stoppedValue.comment:
Given a map `u : ι → Ω → E`, its stopped value with respect to the stopping
time `τ` is the map `x ↦ u (τ ω) ω`.

MeasureTheory.stoppedValue.description: This definition describes a function that assigns a value based on another function that is evaluated at a stopping time, effectively halting the process according to that time.

  (u : ι → Ω → β) (τ : Ω → ι) : ι → Ω → β
MeasureTheory.stoppedProcess.comment:
Given a map `u : ι → Ω → E`, the stopped process with respect to `τ` is `u i ω` if
`i ≤ τ ω`, and `u (τ ω) ω` otherwise.

Intuitively, the stopped process stops evolving once the stopping time has occured.

  [AddCommGroup β] (hle : τ ≤ π) {N : ℕ} (hbdd : ∀ (ω : Ω), π ω ≤ N) :

MeasureTheory.hitting.code:
MeasureTheory.hitting.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [Preorder ι] [InfSet ι]
  (u : ι → Ω → β) (s : Set β) (n m : ι) : Ω → ι
MeasureTheory.hitting.comment:
Hitting time: given a stochastic process `u` and a set `s`, `hitting u s n m` is the first time
`u` is in `s` after time `n` and before time `m` (if `u` does not hit `s` after time `n` and
before `m` then the hitting time is simply `m`).

The hitting time is a stopping time if the process is adapted and discrete.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

MeasureTheory.hitting.fullDefinition: noncomputable def hitting [Preorder ι] [InfSet ι] (u : ι → Ω → β) (s : Set β) (n m : ι) : Ω → ι :=   fun x => if ∃ j ∈ Set.Icc n m, u j x ∈ s then sInf (Set.Icc n m ∩ {i : ι | u i x ∈ s}) else m
MeasureTheory.hitting.description: The definition describes a procedure for determining the first time a stochastic process falls within a specified set after a given start time and before an end time, with a default response if no such event occurs.

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_aux1.code:
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_aux1.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
  (hint : Integrable (X 0) ℙ) (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => IndepFun (X i) (X j) ℙ)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) ℙ ℙ) (hnonneg : ∀ (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ X i ω) {c : ℝ} (c_one : 1 < c)
  {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω),
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      |∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, truncation (X i) (↑i) ω - ∫ (a : Ω), (∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, truncation (X i) ↑i) a| <
        ε * ↑⌊c ^ n⌋₊
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_aux1.comment:
The truncation of `Xᵢ` up to `i` satisfies the strong law of large numbers (with respect to
the truncated expectation) along the sequence `c^n`, for any `c > 1`, up to a given `ε > 0`.
This follows from a variance control.

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_aux7.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
  (hint : Integrable (X 0) ℙ) (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => IndepFun (X i) (X j) ℙ)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) ℙ ℙ) (hnonneg : ∀ (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ X i ω) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω), Tendsto (fun n => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / ↑n) atTop (𝓝 (∫ (a : Ω), X 0 a))
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_aux7.comment:
`Xᵢ` satisfies the strong law of large numbers along all integers. This follows from the
corresponding fact along the sequences `c^n`, and the fact that any integer can be sandwiched
between `c^n` and `c^(n+1)` with comparably small error if `c` is close enough to `1`
(which is formalized in `tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_tendsto_div_floor_pow`).

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_real.code:
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_real.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ] (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
  (hint : Integrable (X 0) ℙ) (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => IndepFun (X i) (X j) ℙ)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) ℙ ℙ) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω), Tendsto (fun n => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / ↑n) atTop (𝓝 (∫ (a : Ω), X 0 a))
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_real.comment:
**Strong law of large numbers**, almost sure version: if `X n` is a sequence of independent
identically distributed integrable real-valued random variables, then `∑ i ∈ range n, X i / n`
converges almost surely to `𝔼[X 0]`. We give here the strong version, due to Etemadi, that only
requires pairwise independence. Superseded by `strong_law_ae`, which works for random variables
taking values in any Banach space.

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_of_measu.code:
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_of_measurable.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (hint : Integrable (X 0) ℙ) (h' : StronglyMeasurable (X 0))
  (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => IndepFun (X i) (X j) ℙ) (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) ℙ ℙ) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω), Tendsto (fun n => (↑n)⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) atTop (𝓝 (∫ (a : Ω), X 0 a))
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_of_measu.comment:
Preliminary lemma for the strong law of large numbers for vector-valued random variables,
assuming measurability in addition to integrability. This is weakened to ae measurability in
the full version `ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae`.

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_of_measu.description: If a sequence of measurable random variables is integrable, pairwise independent, and identically distributed, then almost surely, the average of their sums converges to the integral of the first variable.

ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae.code:
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ] {E : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (X : ℕ → Ω → E)
  (hint : Integrable (X 0) ℙ) (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => IndepFun (X i) (X j) ℙ)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) ℙ ℙ) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω), Tendsto (fun n => (↑n)⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) atTop (𝓝 (∫ (a : Ω), X 0 a))
ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae.comment:
**Strong law of large numbers**, almost sure version: if `X n` is a sequence of independent
identically distributed integrable random variables taking values in a Banach space,
then `n⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ range n, X i` converges almost surely to `𝔼[X 0]`. We give here the strong
version, due to Etemadi, that only requires pairwise independence.

MeasureTheory.Martingale.code:
MeasureTheory.Martingale.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [Preorder ι]
  {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] (f : ι → Ω → E)
  (ℱ : Filtration ι m0) (μ : Measure Ω) : Prop
MeasureTheory.Martingale.comment:
A family of functions `f : ι → Ω → E` is a martingale with respect to a filtration `ℱ` if `f`
is adapted with respect to `ℱ` and for all `i ≤ j`, `μ[f j | ℱ i] =ᵐ[μ] f i`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Adapted: A sequence of functions is considered adapted to a filtration if each function is measurable with respect to the corresponding part of the filtration.

MeasureTheory.Martingale.fullDefinition: def Martingale (f : ι → Ω → E) (ℱ : Filtration ι m0) (μ : Measure Ω) : Prop :=   Adapted ℱ f ∧ ∀ i j, i ≤ j → μ[f j|ℱ i] =ᵐ[μ] f i
MeasureTheory.Martingale.description: The definition characterizes a family of functions as a martingale if it is adapted to a filtration and satisfies the condition of conditional expectation with respect to a measure.

MeasureTheory.predictablePart.comment:
Any `ℕ`-indexed stochastic process can be written as the sum of a martingale and a predictable
process. This is the predictable process. See `martingalePart` for the martingale.

explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.

MeasureTheory.predictablePart.fullDefinition: noncomputable def predictablePart {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} (f : ℕ → Ω → E) (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)     (μ : Measure Ω) : ℕ → Ω → E := fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, μ[f (i + 1) - f i|ℱ i]
MeasureTheory.predictablePart.description: This definition establishes a predictable part of a stochastic process, which can be expressed as a predictable process when decomposed into a martingale and a predictable component.

  ε • μ {ω | ↑ε ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' ⋯ fun k => f k ω} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (∫ (ω : Ω) in {ω | ↑ε ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' ⋯ fun k => f k ω}, f n ω ∂μ)
MeasureTheory.maximal_ineq.comment:
**Doob's maximal inequality**: Given a non-negative submartingale `f`, for all `ε : ℝ≥0`,
we have `ε • μ {ε ≤ f* n} ≤ ∫ ω in {ε ≤ f* n}, f n` where `f* n ω = max_{k ≤ n}, f k ω`.

In some literature, the Doob's maximal inequality refers to what we call Doob's Lp inequality
(which is a corollary of this lemma and will be proved in an upcomming PR).

MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_ae_cond.comment:

is measurable with respect to `⨆ n, ℱ n` where `ℱ` is a filtration, the martingale defined by
`𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges almost everywhere to `g`.

This martingale also converges to `g` in L¹ and this result is provided by
`MeasureTheory.Integrable.tendsto_snorm_condexp`

MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condexp.code:
MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condexp.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} {ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0}
  [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (g : Ω → ℝ) : ∀ᵐ (x : Ω) ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => (μ[g|↑ℱ n]) x) atTop (𝓝 ((μ[g|⨆ n, ↑ℱ n]) x))
MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condexp.comment:
**Lévy's upward theorem**, almost everywhere version: given a function `g` and a filtration
`ℱ`, the sequence defined by `𝔼[g | ℱ n]` converges almost everywhere to `𝔼[g | ⨆ n, ℱ n]`.

MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condexp.description: This theorem states that for a given function and filtration, the sequence of conditional expectations converges almost everywhere to the conditional expectation with respect to the supremum of the filtration.

MeasureTheory.tendsto_sum_indicator_atTop_iff'.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
  {ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {s : ℕ → Set Ω} (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ), MeasurableSet (s n)) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,

      Tendsto (fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (μ[(s (k + 1)).indicator 1|↑ℱ k]) ω) atTop atTop

MeasureTheory.ae_mem_limsup_atTop_iff.code:
MeasureTheory.ae_mem_limsup_atTop_iff.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0}
  (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {s : ℕ → Set Ω} (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ), MeasurableSet (s n)) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
    ω ∈ limsup s atTop ↔ Tendsto (fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (μ[(s (k + 1)).indicator 1|↑ℱ k]) ω) atTop atTop
MeasureTheory.ae_mem_limsup_atTop_iff.comment:
**Lévy's generalization of the Borel-Cantelli lemma**: given a sequence of sets `s` and a
filtration `ℱ` such that for all `n`, `s n` is `ℱ n`-measurable, `limsup s atTop` is almost
everywhere equal to the set for which `∑ k, ℙ(s (k + 1) | ℱ k) = ∞`.

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.indep_comap_.code:
ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.indep_comap_natural_of_lt.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ι : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [LinearOrder ι] [mβ : MeasurableSpace β]
  [NormedAddCommGroup β] [BorelSpace β] {f : ι → Ω → β} {i j : ι} (hf : ∀ (i : ι), StronglyMeasurable (f i))
  (hfi : iIndepFun (fun x => mβ) f μ) (hij : i < j) :
  Indep (MeasurableSpace.comap (f j) mβ) (↑(Filtration.natural f hf) i) μ

explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable: A function is considered strongly measurable if it can be approximated as the limit of a sequence of simple functions.
explanatories.ProbabilityTheory.Indep: This definition establishes the independence of two measurable space structures under a measure by requiring that the measure of their intersection equals the product of their individual measures for any selected sets from each structure.
explanatories.MeasurableSpace.comap: This definition describes a measurable space constructed from an existing measurable space by considering the preimages of measurable sets under a function, ensuring that a set is measurable if it corresponds to the preimage of a measurable set in the target space.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Filtration.natural: This definition establishes a natural filtration as the minimal sequence of σ-algebras under which a given sequence of functions is measurable.

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.indep_comap_.description: The theorem establishes that if two functions are independent and one is evaluated at a later index than the other, then their generated σ-algebras remain independent.
